seoTitle: Social Media & Meta Ads for Local Businesses
description: Practical guides to Facebook, Instagram and TikTok marketing for local businesses: organic content, paid ads, costs, tracking and AI tools, in reading order.
intro: This guide collects our articles on social media and Meta advertising for local businesses. It covers organic posting on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok, paid ads, pixel tracking, influencer partnerships, AI scheduling tools and what social advertising tends to cost. It is written for owners of salons, cafes, studios and shops who run marketing themselves and want a clear place to start.

If your budget is small, start with the basics: audit what you post now, pick one platform your customers actually use, and post short video or photos of real work consistently. Read the advertising cost guide before you spend anything, then set up tracking so you can see what your ads produce. Add paid campaigns or influencer partnerships only once organic posts get a response.

Plenty of this can be done yourself, especially organic posting, simple boosted posts and basic scheduling. Help is worth considering when ad spend is meaningful, tracking is broken, or you simply do not have the hours to stay consistent. DataLatte works with local businesses on Meta ads and social media management, but the guides here are meant to stand on their own.

faq.q: Which social media platform is best for a local business?
faq.a: It depends on where your customers already spend time. Instagram suits visual businesses such as salons, bakeries and florists, Facebook still reaches a wide local audience, and TikTok can work well for short, personality-led video. Pick one, do it consistently, and add another later.

faq.q: How much should a small business spend on social media ads?
faq.a: There is no single right number. Many local businesses start with a modest monthly test budget, then raise it only after they can see ads leading to calls, bookings or sales. Our cost guide explains what drives prices up or down so you can set a realistic starting point.

faq.q: Do I need the Facebook pixel to run Meta ads?
faq.a: You can run ads without it, but you will have a hard time knowing what they actually achieve. The pixel lets Meta record actions such as form submissions or purchases on your website. Setting it up early makes every later campaign easier to judge and improve.

faq.q: Can AI tools manage my social media for me?
faq.a: AI can speed up drafting captions, planning a calendar and scheduling posts. It works less well at capturing your real shop, your staff and your local voice. Most small businesses get the best results using AI as an assistant while a person still reviews and posts the genuine photos and videos.
